profilePosition: A thin, versioned, JSON/YAML-compatible experimental profile for source-visible authorization and trust-boundary assessment. It compiles to instructions and existing ledger/SARIF artifacts; it is not a general security-review language, a new CLI, a security engine, or a replacement result format.
currentRecommendation: Use bounded rendering only as the profile arm of a paired method probe against existing configuration plus the same helper. No consumption mode is yet shown superior, and the profile is not a default implementation recommendation.

interfaceAudit.reuse: Existing loader resolves a normal skill and resources; buildSkillBundleFromContent can carry deterministic rendered content without creating a new skill format.
interfaceAudit.gap: The ordinary executeRun interface accepts ResolvedSkill rather than a prebuilt SkillBundle, so a no-production-change probe should materialize a temporary rendered SKILL.md instead of duplicating the run lifecycle.

interfaceAudit.reuse: Existing lifecycle copies fixtures, captures optional pre-run bytes before skill deployment, deploys canonical bundle resources, invokes the adapter, and returns RunResult.
interfaceAudit.gap: prepareRunWorkspaceArtifacts is private and the CLI non-opt path does not expose preRunInputSnapshotPath; a development library caller can use executeRun directly.

interfaceAudit.reuse: Skill injection/discovery, adapter execution, canonical run status, usage, steps, and four existing evaluation modes already cover the generic runtime surface.
interfaceAudit.gap: No domain-profile/result field belongs in RunResult; keep security artifacts as files and evaluator inputs.

interfaceAudit.reuse: Inject mode embeds rendered skill text; discover mode exposes skill metadata and deployed resources; logging and runtime trace are already threaded.
interfaceAudit.gap: The fixed tool set includes write_file, execute_command, and web_fetch and has no per-run allowlist. A profile instruction cannot guarantee source-only/no-network execution.

interfaceAudit.reuse: Existing provider routing remains the single chokepoint for model configuration.
interfaceAudit.gap: None specific to the profile; route availability and cost telemetry remain runtime facts.

interfaceAudit.reuse: Existing typed model envelope supports tool-use first and prompt/parse fallback with accumulated fallback tokens and cost.
interfaceAudit.gap: It is only needed if a later bounded interpreter call is justified; ordinary rendered-skill consumption should not introduce an extra model call.

interfaceAudit.reuse: Script/file/custom/LLM evaluation and usage hooks already exist; custom is the declared extension point for domain evaluation.
interfaceAudit.gap: The built-in JSON-schema file check validates only a basic subset and cannot prove evidence/coverage cross-references; a pure profile validator or later custom evaluator is needed.

interfaceAudit.reuse: Captures original workdir bytes and digests before skill resources are deployed, with size caps and omission reasons.
interfaceAudit.gap: Large files can be omitted; an experiment must disclose the captured denominator rather than treating a snapshot reference as complete repository evidence.

interfaceAudit.reuse: Can bind initial state and constrain expected result artifacts in a development evaluator.
interfaceAudit.gap: It validates file deltas, not security semantics.

interfaceAudit.reuse: Provides run-scoped provider/tool/turn timing and termination events.
interfaceAudit.gap: Events summarize tool types and counts, not domain evidence; profile artifacts remain necessary.

now: Do not add a CLI or production route in this research round.

For the next minimal implementation, keep a development-only authorization-profile parser/resolver/renderer/result-validator, an equivalent existing-config adapter using the same semantic helper, and two small public source fixtures.
Materialize a temporary ordinary skill directory with rendered SKILL.md plus profile and seeded ledger resources, then call existing executeRun from a development runner.

Use the same helper, model, inputs, validators, one generation, and at most one actionable repair across existing-config+ledger and profile-rendered conditions; organized Markdown remains an optional descriptive baseline.
Run no real model until a per-run source-only tool boundary is explicit; otherwise record the boundary as prompt-only and do not claim sandboxed audit behavior.
